items.prompt:
In a group discussion, you should speak _____ at a time.
A) everyone
B) one person

steps: Only one person should speak at a time so that everyone can hear and be heard.

items.prompt:
When a classmate is talking, you should:
A) Talk over them
B) Listen carefully

steps: Listening carefully is a key rule of collaborative conversations.

items.prompt:
If you do not understand what someone said, you should:
A) Stay quiet
B) Ask a question

steps: Asking a question to clear up confusion is an important conversation rule.

items.prompt:
Ana says, 'I like dogs.' Ben says, 'Me too! My dog can do tricks.' Is Ben building on Ana's comment?
A) Yes
B) No

steps: Ben agrees and adds a connected idea about dogs. He is building on Ana's comment.

items.prompt:
Which is a good conversation rule?
A) Interrupt people so they know you have an idea.
B) Wait for your turn before speaking.
items.answer: B) Wait for your turn before speaking.

steps: Waiting for a turn is a basic, important conversation rule.

items.prompt:
Sam is talking about his favorite book. Jake starts talking about his lunch. Is Jake following good conversation rules?
A) Yes
B) No

steps: Jake is changing the topic instead of staying on the current topic (favorite books). This is not a good conversation behavior.

items.prompt:
A student listens to her partner and then says, 'I agree with you because...' What is she doing?
A) Building on her partner's idea
B) Changing the subject
items.answer: A) Building on her partner's idea

steps: Saying 'I agree with you because...' connects to what the partner said and adds to it — that is building on others' talk.

items.prompt:
During a discussion, a student has a great idea. She should:
A) Shout it out immediately
B) Wait for a pause and then share her idea
items.answer: B) Wait for a pause and then share her idea

steps: Good conversation rules include gaining the floor in a respectful way by waiting for a natural pause.

items.prompt:
Two students are having a conversation. Student A says, 'I like the color blue.' Student B says, 'I like the color blue, too!' Is this a good response?
A) Yes — Student B listened and connected her idea
B) No — Student B should talk about something else

steps: Student B listened and shared a connected idea. This is a simple but valid conversational response.

items.prompt:
What does it mean to 'listen with care' in a conversation?
A) Looking away and thinking about other things
B) Paying attention to every word the speaker says
items.answer: B) Paying attention to every word the speaker says

steps: 'Listening with care' (from CCSS 1.SL.A.1a) means giving full attention to the speaker.

items.prompt:
Mia says, 'My cat is fluffy.' Leo says, 'I have a fish.' Is Leo building on Mia's comment?
A) Yes — he is talking about animals
B) No — he is changing the subject from cats specifically
items.answer: A) Yes — he is talking about animals

steps: While not perfectly connected, Leo is staying on a related topic (pets/animals). At Grade 1, this is acceptable — he is not completely off-topic.

items.prompt:
Which is the BEST question to ask a classmate after she shares about her weekend?
A) 'What did you do on Saturday?'
B) 'What is your favorite color?'
items.answer: A) 'What did you do on Saturday?'

steps: Option A asks about the topic under discussion (her weekend). Option B changes topics completely.

items.prompt:
True or False: In a good conversation, one person does ALL the talking.
A) True
B) False

steps: A good collaborative conversation involves everyone participating and taking turns.

items.prompt:
A student says, 'I think the story had a happy ending.' A classmate says, 'I disagree. The ending was sad for the rabbit.' Is this a good conversation behavior?
A) No — disagreeing is not allowed.
B) Yes — respectfully sharing a different opinion is a good conversation skill.

steps: Respectfully disagreeing and explaining your thinking is a positive conversation skill. Conversations can include different opinions.

items.prompt:
Which of these is a rule for a good group discussion?
A) Whisper so only one person can hear you.
B) Listen to others, speak one at a time, and ask questions.
items.answer: B) Listen to others, speak one at a time, and ask questions.

steps: These three behaviors — listening, taking turns, and asking questions — are the core rules of collaborative conversation (1.SL.A.1).
